clue.text: Audition viably arranged, characteristic of a certain event

indicators.note: letters arranged are put into a new order, so the two words Audition viably are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A talent show's casting call is set up in a way that seems somehow fated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain' here means sure to happen, not 'particular': a sure event has the quality of being inescapable.
explanation.definitionFit: An event that is certain to happen cannot be escaped, and that inescapability is its defining quality.

clue.text: Things look bad after this fruit lies around area

parts.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine

indicators.note: the word for lies goes around the letter for area, holding it inside

parts.note: lies are fiction, things made up

explanation.surface: Some overripe fruit left lying in a spot spoils the view.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the Mock Turtle's four branches of arithmetic in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland (Ambition, Distraction, Uglification and Derision), a pun on multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something ugly leaves it looking bad afterwards, so the process is described by its result.

clue.text: Calculating type found in snakes and ladders?

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits inside the clue's letters, here inside the word ladders

explanation.surface: The children's board game of snakes and ladders, with a nod to a counting player.
explanation.walkthrough: An adder is also a snake, so the answer sits among the snakes as well as inside 'ladders'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that adds up figures is a calculator, a person or machine that does sums.

clue.text: Possibility, over time, for job in theatre

indicators.note: the word for possibility lies over, spread across, the word for time, enclosing it

parts.note: an option is a possibility, one choice open to you
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An actor weighs a chance of work in theatre, with time running on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is the operating theatre of a hospital, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery done in an operating theatre is a surgical procedure, a surgeon's piece of work.

clue.text: Oxford mathematician is evasive about subtracting transcendental number

indicators.note: subtracting means taking away, so the number's letter is removed from the word for being evasive

parts.note: someone who is evasive dodges
e, the base of natural logarithms, is a famous transcendental number
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A slippery Oxford don avoids a tricky number.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Dodgson taught mathematics at Christ Church, Oxford, and wrote as Lewis Carroll (23 across).
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lutwidge Dodgson was a mathematics lecturer at Christ Church, Oxford, better known by his pen name.

clue.text: Save man on board threatened by mate that's crazy

parts.note: save means except, as does bar: 'all bar one'

parts.words: man on board threatened by mate
parts.note: in chess the king is the piece that checkmate threatens

explanation.surface: A chess player rescues a piece in danger of checkmate with a mad move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for mad, short for 'barking mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang barking, short for barking mad, means completely insane.

clue.text: Learner isn't turning one letter around for composer

parts.note: L is for learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: one letter of the word is turned a quarter of the way around, which makes a different letter shape

parts.note: isn't is written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A student refuses to spin round for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn the N of ISNT through 90 degrees and it becomes a Z, giving ISZT.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Decisive defeat in ring — count out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer loses decisively when the referee counts him out in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouncing is a thorough beating, a defeat leaving no doubt about the winner.

clue.text: Horizontal surface in which line meets side

indicators.note: meets means one piece joins the next, side by side

parts.note: an edge is a side or border

explanation.surface: A geometry description of a flat plane where a line touches a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow flat shelf projecting from a wall or cliff.

clue.text: Ridicule resolution to replace Conservative by monarch

indicators.note: to replace signals one letter being swapped out of the word
by names what the swapped letter is replaced with

parts.note: a decision is a resolution, a firm choice made
R is for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A political motion to swap a Tory for a king draws mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: Another of the Mock Turtle's branches of arithmetic in Alice in Wonderland, a pun on division.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is scornful mockery, the act of laughing at someone with contempt.

clue.text: Circle and lines artist arranged for some language experts

parts.note: O is circle-shaped

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of lines and artist are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An artist lays out circles and lines for a team of linguists.
explanation.definitionFit: Orientalists are scholars of Eastern cultures, including Asian languages such as Arabic or Chinese.

clue.text: Designs in place of words repeatedly found in mathematics

parts.note: for means in place of, as in swapping one for another
the word mat appears twice in mathematics, at the start and in the middle, so the plural

explanation.surface: Patterns turning up again and again in maths formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: Formats are layouts or arrangements, the designs in which material is set out.

clue.text: Using modified ten iron, his pitch changes little

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters of ten iron are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer with an altered club finds his shots hardly vary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a golf shot to suit the iron, but it is the pitch of the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who chants in a monotone keeps his voice at almost one musical level.

clue.text: Measure of interest in group of islands, or one

indicators.note: in places the interest figure inside the island group's letters

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands
APR, annual percentage rate, measures the interest on a loan

explanation.surface: A tourist asks about interest in an island group, or a single island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the definition: one island, like the group just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a single island in the Bay of Naples, one island by itself.

clue.text: Send carriage that's turned up for one not fully engaged

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to remit is to send, as with money
a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone sends off a carriage that has overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-time worker is employed for only some of the working week, never a full-time job.

clue.text: Activity at club following being swamped in 8-0 disaster

indicators.note: being swamped in means sinking inside, so one letter goes into the middle of the others
a disaster is a mess, so the spelt-out score is jumbled

parts.note: eight-nil spelt out, a football scoreline
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A football club's fans endure an eight-nil thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a football team after an 8-0 result, but it is a nightclub. Rearrange EIGHT NIL to NIGHTLIE and swamp F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightlife is the evening entertainment of bars and clubs, what people do after dark.

clue.text: Article concerning appetite heartlessly impractical

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: heartlessly means losing the heart, the central letter of the word

parts.note: orectic is a rare adjective meaning to do with appetite or desire

explanation.surface: A cruel newspaper piece about someone's hunger comes across as unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: ORECTIC, from Greek orexis, means relating to appetite; drop its central C to get ORETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something theoretic belongs to theory rather than practice, so it is not practical.

clue.text: Like woeful number produced by adding constant to one third, oddly

indicators.note: adding means one piece is joined on to the other, here at the end
oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, notably the speed of light

explanation.surface: A maths problem adds a constant to one third with peculiar results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song or poem, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament or dirge, so threnodic describes a mournful song.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement putting barrier around platform

indicators.note: the barrier goes around the platform, enclosing it

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across a river
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: Protesters build a barricade around the speaker's stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics; Dadaism was a revolutionary art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Dadaism was an early twentieth-century art movement that overturned artistic conventions.

clue.text: Fair target after company falsified count

indicators.note: falsified means faked, so the letters of count are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm cooks the books, and becomes a fair target for criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' means a funfair: at a coconut shy you throw balls to knock coconuts off stands.
explanation.definitionFit: At a British funfair coconut shy, the coconut is the thing players throw balls at.

clue.text: For this cube, what's subtracted from vertical measurement when it's minimised?

definitions.text: For this cube, what's subtracted from vertical measurement when it's minimised?

parts.words: For this cube, what's subtracted from vertical measurement when it's minimised?
parts.note: a cube number; taking its spelt-out letters away from the word for vertical measurement leaves just that word's first letter, the measurement at its smallest

explanation.walkthrough: Eight is two cubed. HEIGHT minus EIGHT leaves just H, so the vertical measurement is cut down to one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Two multiplied by itself three times gives this number, so it is a perfect cube.

clue.text: Marine creature's head swallowed by old fish

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside, so the head goes into the fish

parts.note: the cod is a fish
top means head, the uppermost part

explanation.surface: An elderly fish gulps down another sea creature's head.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopod is an eight-limbed cephalopod such as the octopus, living in the sea.

clue.text: Use digit or what may be between digits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to use a finger to indicate
second meaning: a decimal ... sits between figures, as in 3.14

explanation.walkthrough: 'digit' means a finger in the first part and a numeral in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To point is to indicate with a finger; a decimal point separates the whole number from fractions.

clue.text: Writer of nonsensical verse both sides repeated in song

indicators.note: both sides are right and left, R and L; repeated means each of those letters in the word for song is written twice

parts.note: a carol is a song, especially at Christmas

explanation.surface: A poet writes absurd lines with the refrain repeated on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: CAROL already holds an R and an L; doubling both sides, right and left, gives CARROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll wrote Jabberwocky and The Hunting of the Snark, famous nonsense poems.

clue.text: Nothing tops excellent end of series

indicators.note: in a down clue tops means one piece sits above the next

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
mega is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A TV review says nothing beats a brilliant season finale.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the final item.

clue.text: Reordered mini, alternating with sailor, to drive

indicators.note: reordered means put into another order, so the letters of mini are shuffled
alternating with means the letters are interleaved one by one with the other pieces

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A rejigged Mini, swapping drivers with a sailor, is taken for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Reorder MINI as MIIN and interleave it with AB and TO: A-M-B-I-T-I-O-N. A Mock Turtle branch of arithmetic, a pun on addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is drive, the strong desire to succeed and get ahead.

clue.text: Numbers around end of score (for bigger numbers under score)

indicators.note: around means the numbers go round the letter

parts.note: tens are numbers, multiples of ten

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word score

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's maths exercise counts up towards twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty; the bigger numbers under it are thirteen to nineteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The teens run from thirteen to nineteen, the larger numbers below twenty, a score.

clue.text: They can handle distraction as well as 25, 1 down, and 9, according to 23

definitions.text: They can handle distraction as well as 25, 1 down, and 9, according to 23

parts.words: They can handle distraction as well as 25, 1 down, and 9, according to 23
parts.note: Carroll's Mock Turtle names Ambition, Distraction, Uglification and Derision as the four branches of arithmetic, so people skilled in that subject handle all four

explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland the Mock Turtle's schooling covered Ambition, Distraction, Uglification and Derision, puns on addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts in sums deal with the four operations, which Carroll's Mock Turtle renamed as these jokes.
